newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa slips in last-minute fund sales.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa slips in last-minute fund sales.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures slipped further just before the Monday close in fast dealing marked by a series of fund sales, traders said.
"It was a busy finish. The funds were selling because of a weak close," said one trader.
Last minute offers followed mild sales earlier in the session which traders linked to Ivorian shippers' coupled with modest scale-down industry buying.
But Monday's activity was relatively narrow as the market seemed to be retreating into a seasonal lull.
But despite the closing rush of sales, the day's volume was still a modest 3,046 lots, including over 900 lots of AAs and crosses, traders said.
Benchmark March cocoa ended six stg down on the day at 914 stg a tonne after touching a session low of 910 stg. Other positions lost up to six stg.
Traders said fund selling appeared to be of technical nature in the absence of any physical news. It could have been triggered by a break of nearby support of 915 stg basis March.
Technically, the next level of crucial support is 900 stg on March, analysts said.
"If 900 stg is broken, the fall could extend to 880," said technical analyst Elli Gifford at Investment Research of Cambridge.
